construction_markdown: No leaderboard construction is claimed. This result formalizes the narrow certificate class consisting of a one-point GS evaluation code over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\), the inner code \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), ordinary symbolwise concatenation, designed outer distance, bare Riemann–Roch dimension credit, product-distance analysis, and zero padding. It proves the advertised asymptotic envelope and gives exact conditions under which a stronger outer tradeoff or inner code would escape it.
distance_audit: The inner code \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\) has length \(2^{m-1}\), dimension \(m\), and minimum distance \(2^{m-2}\): every nonconstant affine function is balanced, while the nonzero constant function has full weight.

For every nonzero outer word, at least \(D\) symbols are nonzero. Injectivity of the inner map sends each such symbol to a nonzero inner word of weight at least \(d\); disjoint coordinate blocks therefore give weight at least \(Dd\).
With the RM inner code, the relative product bound is \(\delta_{\rm bin}\ge \Delta_{\rm out}/2\), so the target \(7/16\) forces \(\Delta_{\rm out}\ge7/8\) in an unpadded construction.
At fixed length \(2^{30}\), the exact required outer distance for \(m=8\) is \(469,762,048/64=7,340,032\). This uses the final padded length, not merely the unpadded relative distance.
Designed distance and the concatenation product are lower bounds only. An actual-distance bonus or a symbol-distribution argument is outside the proved barrier.

For \(m=30\), the exact outer-distance requirement is \(\lceil7/4\rceil=2\); the simplified \(7L/8\) expression is not valid there. For even \(m\ge32\), one unpunctured inner block is already longer than \(2^{30}\).
explicitness_audit: This is a deterministic symbolic ceiling lemma, not a code construction; no random existence or sampled-word argument is used.
All target, inner-code, padding, dimension, and distance arithmetic is exact.
No finite GS level satisfying the escape condition is asserted, and no unavailable special divisor is assumed.
The asymptotic expression is explicitly not presented as a pointwise upper bound on finite GS-derived codes.
No repository files were changed because this response is an obstruction/proof-tool result rather than a leaderboard submission.

obstructions: The advertised formula optimizes a lower-bound proof calculus. Riemann–Roch, designed distance, and product distance do not upper-bound the corresponding actual parameters.
There is no uniquely weakest hypothesis under logical implication: stronger inner tradeoffs, stronger outer tradeoffs, and better concatenated-distance analyses are independent escapes.
Holding every other ingredient fixed at m=8, the smallest quantitative escape is any strict outer-rate gain over 7/120 at outer relative distance at least 7/8.
At the concrete verified level, an infinitesimal asymptotic gain is not enough: its certified aggregate genus-plus-padding loss must improve by 28,280 outer dimensions.
At m=8, merely replacing [128,8,64] by a hypothetical [128,8,65] inner code is impossible by the Plotkin bound; an inner-only escape must change the joint length-distance tradeoff.

proof_markdown:
### Vanilla GS–Hadamard certificate barrier

Let \(m\in2\mathbb Z_{>0}\), put
\[
h=2^{m-1},\qquad d_0=2^{m-2},\qquad q=2^{m/2},\qquad \gamma_m=\frac1{q-1}.
\]
Consider outer evaluation codes of length \(L_j\), genus \(g_j\), and divisor degree \(a_j\), concatenated with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)=[h,m,d_0]_2\). Let the concatenated word be zero-padded to length \(n_j\ge hL_j\), and write
\[
\lambda_j=\frac{hL_j}{n_j}\le1.
\]
Assume that distance is certified only through
\[
d_0(L_j-a_j)\ge\frac7{16}n_j,
\tag{1}
\]
that \(\liminf_j(g_j-1)/L_j\ge\gamma_m\), and that credited outer dimension is only \([a_j+1-g_j]_+\). The same conclusion applies to actual dimensions if the specialness \(i(G_j)=\ell(K_j-G_j)=o(L_j)\).

From (1) and \(d_0=h/2\),
\[
\frac{\lambda_j}{2}\left(1-\frac{a_j}{L_j}\right)\ge\frac7{16},
\qquad
\frac{a_j}{L_j}\le1-\frac7{8\lambda_j}.
\]
Consequently the credited binary rate satisfies
\[
R_j^{\rm cert}
=\frac{m[a_j+1-g_j]_+}{n_j}
\le
\frac m h\left[
\lambda_j\left(1-\frac{g_j-1}{L_j}\right)-\frac78
\right]_+.
\]
Because \(\lambda_j\le1\), taking the limsup gives
\[
\limsup_jR_j^{\rm cert}
\le
\frac m{2^{m-1}}
\left(\frac18-\frac1{2^{m/2}-1}\right)_+.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus zero padding cannot improve the envelope. The [Garcia–Stichtenoth tower theorem](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01884295) supplies the limiting ratio used in (2).

### Optimization over every positive even m

For \(m=2,4,6\), one has \(1/(2^{m/2}-1)\ge1/7>1/8\), so (2) is zero. At \(m=8\),
\[
R_{\rm template}(8)
=\frac8{128}\left(\frac18-\frac1{15}\right)
=\frac1{16}\cdot\frac7{120}
=\frac7{1920}.
\]
For every even \(m\ge10\),
\[
R_{\rm template}(m)<\frac m{2^{m+2}}.
\]
The latter quantity decreases along even integers because
\[
\frac{(m+2)/2^{m+4}}{m/2^{m+2}}=\frac{m+2}{4m}<1.
\]
Therefore
\[
R_{\rm template}(m)<\frac{10}{2^{12}}= rac5{2048}<\frac7{1920}.
\]
Hence \(m=8\) is the unique maximizer.

### Scope audit

Riemann–Roch actually gives
\[
\ell(G)=\deg G+1-g+i(G),\qquad i(G)\ge0,
\]
not an upper bound \(\ell(G)\le\deg G+1-g\). Likewise, \(L-\deg G\) and the concatenation product are only lower bounds on distance. Finally, \((g-1)/L\to1/(q-1)\) is asymptotic rather than a finite pointwise inequality. Thus (2) is an upper bound on what this restricted certificate credits, not on all actual GS-derived codes.

### Minimal aggregate escape

Keep \(m=8\), the \([128,8,64]\) inner code, ordinary concatenation, no padding, and product-distance certification. An outer code with rate \(\rho\) and relative distance \(\Delta\) gives binary rate \(\rho/16\) and certified relative distance \(\Delta/2\). It crosses the envelope exactly when
\[
\Delta\ge\frac78,
\qquad
\rho>16\cdot\frac7{1920}=\frac7{120}.
\tag{3}
\]
The bare RR line attains equality in (3). Therefore, holding all other hypotheses fixed, any strict certified outer-rate improvement at this point suffices. This is the smallest quantitative single relaxation, although stronger-inner and better-distance arguments are logically incomparable alternatives.

For a general unpadded binary inner code \([\ell,m,d]_2\), the same outer line credits
\[
\Phi_m(\ell,d)=
\frac m\ell
\left(1-\gamma_m-\frac{7\ell}{16d}\right)_+.
\]
It escapes precisely when \(\Phi_m(\ell,d)>7/1920\). At \(m=8\), this becomes
\[
d>\frac{960\ell}{2048-\ell}.
\tag{4}
\]
The standard pair \((\ell,d)=(128,64)\) is exactly on the boundary.

### Exact finite m=8 audit

Let
\[
T=\frac{2^{30}}{128}=2^{23}=8,388,608,
\qquad L=T-p.
\]
The required outer distance is
\[
D=\frac{469,762,048}{64}=7,340,032=\frac78T.
\]
Choosing the largest divisor degree permitted by designed distance and using a certified genus upper bound \(\bar g\) gives
\[
K_{\rm RR}=L-D+1-\bar g
=\frac T8-(p+\bar g-1).
\tag{5}
\]
A general binary code first crosses \(7/1920\) at dimension \(3,914,684\). Since an \(m=8\) concatenated dimension is divisible by eight, it must instead have
\[
k\ge3,914,688,
\qquad K\ge489,336.
\]
Substituting into (5), bare RR accounting crosses exactly when
\[
p+\bar g-1\le559,240.
\tag{6}
\]
For the verified GS baseline,
\[
p=32,768,
\qquad \bar g=554,753,
\qquad p+\bar g-1=587,520.
\]
It is therefore \(587,520-559,240=28,280\) certified outer dimensions short of crossing the asymptotic envelope. No theorem in the reviewed records supplies those dimensions, so this audit produces no new leaderboard code.

research_direction: Treat 7/1920 as the optimum of the asymptotic vanilla RR/designed-distance/product certificate. The quantitatively smallest escape at the maximizing alphabet is an outer F_256 point with relative distance at least 7/8 and rate strictly greater than 7/120; at the current finite level this requires 28,280 additional certified outer dimensions. Stronger inner codes must satisfy the displayed joint length-distance inequality.
theorem_statement: For every positive even m, the asymptotic one-level GS plus RM(1,m−1) certificate that uses only bare Riemann–Roch dimension, designed outer distance, product concatenation distance, and zero padding has certified rate at relative distance 7/16 at most R_template(m)=(m/2^(m−1))(1/8−1/(2^(m/2)−1))_+. This expression has the unique maximum 7/1920 at m=8. It is not an upper bound on actual GS-derived codes. Holding m=8, RM(1,7), ordinary concatenation, and product-distance analysis fixed, crossing is equivalent in the unpadded asymptotic calculation to certifying an outer F_256 code with relative distance at least 7/8 and rate greater than 7/120.
